subject: A2D5016F2A87467E87D0D1509478C894
introduction: The Hands of the Cause of God were individuals appointed, first by Bahá’u’lláh and later by Shoghi Effendi, to teach, to encourage and to protect the Bahá’í community; they held rank without executive power, and after the last appointments in 1957 no more can be made. This guide gathers what was written to and about them. The qualities asked are those of servants: learning, detachment, constancy. Paul’s lists of gifts and his “stewards of the mysteries”, Aaron and Hur holding up the hands of Moses, and Jesus’s rule that the great must be the minister of all are the precedents. His “be not ye called Rabbi” and Ezekiel’s shepherds are the warnings that attach to every honoured office.
questions: What were the Hands of the Cause for? What did they lack that an elected body has, and why?
How can a community honour individuals of distinction without creating a clergy?
What do the readings ask of those honoured, as distinct from those who honour them?

outside.why: The Hands of the Cause are to be appointed by the Guardian. He gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; for the edifying of the body.
Souls who have abandoned their own desires. Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee.
The hosts of Truth are the Hands of His Cause. Aaron and Hur stayed up Moses’ hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side.
Their first duties are to write and to teach. Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
The educators of the servants. They that turn many to righteousness shall shine as the stars for ever and ever.
God has chosen you for His servitude. Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God.
Not a title to be bestowed at will, nor a seat. Whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister.
Jesus forbade titles among his followers: be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, and all ye are brethren. How do the readings guard a title of honour from becoming what he feared?
Show the utmost consideration to the Hands. Obey them that have the rule over you: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account.
From every direction rises the cry, “Where are the teachers?” How shall they hear without a preacher?
Whatever the Hands deem advisable must be carried out. When ye shall have done all, say, we are unprofitable servants. What attitude toward their own authority do the readings ask of those given it?
The Hands firm in the Covenant are the lamps of the horizons. Among whom ye shine as lights in the world.

Ezekiel on appointed leaders who failed: woe be to the shepherds that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks? What in the readings’ description of the Hands is the safeguard against that?

shortfall: Seventy further readings are messages to and about particular Hands of the Cause and later institutional guidance.
